title: Coherent localization comparison for exact inverse image
statement:
Let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a geometric morphism between sheaf topoi on small sites, meaning an adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ whose inverse image preserves finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal Y$ and let $t$ be a global section. Put $R'=f^{-1}R$ and $t'=f^{-1}t$. Module sheaves, sheafified localization and ordinary unbounded derived categories are as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On modules set $M[1/t]=R[1/t]\otimes_R M$, using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There are canonical ring and module isomorphisms
$$f^{-1}(R[1/t])\cong R'[1/t'],\qquad \beta_{f,M}:f^{-1}(M[1/t])\xrightarrow{\sim}(f^{-1}M)[1/t'].$$
They preserve the localization units and on local fraction representatives send $m/t^n$ to the inverse-image representative of $m$ divided by $(t')^n$. Both module inverse image with these identified rings and scalar localization are exact. Their termwise derived functors therefore have the same natural comparison $\beta_f$, with no bound on the complex. For another geometric morphism $g:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X$, the comparison for $f\circ g$ is the composite of $g^{-1}\beta_f$ and $\beta_g$ after inserting the canonical inverse-image composition isomorphisms on source and target; the identity comparison is the identity under the canonical identity inverse image. These are equations of natural transformations, including their derived versions. The comparison also commutes with a specified identification $f^{-1}R\cong S$ by a ring-sheaf isomorphism and the induced identification of the scalar sections.
